text: Univariate just means one variable at a time. Before you compare columns to each other, you need to know what each one looks like on its own: where it's centered, how spread out it is, what shape it takes, and whether anything looks off.

For every numeric column, ask four questions: center, spread, shape, oddities. Numbers answer some of these, but a histogram answers all four at once. Age is roughly bell-shaped, balanced around the late thirties. Tenure months has a long right tail: most customers are new, a few have stuck around for years.

Total spend looks like one bar near zero plus a couple of dots far to the right. The histogram is telling you something is extreme, and skew puts a number on it. Age scores point one eight, nearly symmetric. Tenure scores one point three six. Orders, one point one three. Total spend: fifteen point oh three, dramatically skewed by two huge values.

Compare center measures too. Total spend's median is one twenty-four point four, but its mean is one eighty-eight point one. When a distribution is right-skewed, the mean gets dragged toward the tail, so the median is usually the better typical value.

Quantiles show how thin that tail really is. Fifty, ninety, and ninety-nine percent come out to one twenty-four point four, three oh seven point nine, and six sixty-nine point six. So ninety-nine percent of customers spend under about six seventy, yet two rows sit at seventy-four hundred and ninety-eight hundred. Those two aren't the tail; they're suspects.

For categories, count them, and use proportions too. Regions: North one fifty, East one forty-four, West one oh seven, South ninety-nine. Channels: web forty-seven percent, store thirty-four, app nineteen. Watch for rare categories, dominant categories, and spelling variants that value_counts reveals immediately.

Look at center, spread, shape and oddities for every numeric column; histograms reveal what summary statistics can hide. With right skew, trust the median over the mean. Next: bivariate analysis, comparing two variables at a time.
